decisions.reason: The quota already states that only personally approved clips count; sending rejected clips back for correction changes the approval workflow but not the quota value or counting rule.
The rejected-clip handling decision does not necessarily change the future Lead Clipper role, training pathway, compensation, or responsibilities.
The source establishes correction handling for clips in the monthly production role, not a change to the completed qualification method or its success condition.
Returning a substandard clip for correction does not change the existing project-chat submission channel or the task-local sample submission content.
The publishing requirement already limits publication to client-approved clips; correction of rejected clips does not change the publishable status criterion or Instagram destination.
The source mentions moment selection as prospective training content but does not alter the current moment-selection standard.
The general rule for returning noncompliant clips does not modify the established caption color, font, or effects requirements.
The rejection-and-correction workflow does not change which source content may be used for clips.
The source does not change the established 30-to-90-second duration range.
The source promises training about editing style but does not change the existing clean, simple, no-effects, and no-transitions standard.
The source does not modify the requirement that clips contain complete standalone lessons or stories; it only establishes handling for clips that fail the broader approval standard.
